mathgap.title: Signed Equality for Difference Statements
mathgap.principle: When a statement equates two differences, treat both sides as signed equations preserving the order; i.e., interpret 'A has more than B equals C has more than D' as (A - B) = (C - D).
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement says the number of tomatoes that X has more than Y equals the difference between the number of tomatoes that U and V have.
mathgap.example: Interpreting such a statement as |A - B| = |C - D| or swapping sides, which loses the sign and yields incorrect equations.

mathgap.title: Iterative Substitution and Propagation
mathgap.principle: Whenever a variable's value becomes known (through a direct count, a solved equation, or a transfer), substitute that value into all other equations and update dependent variables, repeating until no further propagation is possible.
mathgap.when_to_apply: After any equation or count is resolved, propagate the known value throughout the system.
mathgap.example: Failing to substitute a newly known count into other equations, leaving them unsolved or using outdated values.

mathgap.title: Chronological Evaluation of Comparative Statements
mathgap.principle: Evaluate each comparative statement using the counts as they exist at that point in the text, after applying any earlier direct counts, transfers, or other updates.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When processing a 'has K more/fewer than' or difference equality statement, use the current values of the involved persons at that moment.
mathgap.example: Treating a comparative statement as if it referred to the initial counts, ignoring earlier transfers that changed the counts.

mathgap.title: Query‑Focused Subsystem Extraction
mathgap.principle: Identify the minimal subset of equations and variables that are directly or indirectly connected to the queried person, and ignore unrelated statements.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Before solving, trace connections from the query target through all statements to isolate the relevant subsystem.
mathgap.example: Attempting to solve the entire large system, including many irrelevant variables, leading to confusion or misapplied constraints.

mathgap.title: Distinct Name Disambiguation
mathgap.principle: Treat each unique name as a separate variable, even if names differ by only a single character; avoid conflating them.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When parsing statements, ensure that similarly spelled names are not merged.
mathgap.example: Confusing 'Chester' with 'Chest' or merging 'Susanna' and 'Susana' into one variable, causing incorrect equations.

mathgap.title: Preserve Order in "Difference Between" Phrases
mathgap.principle: When a phrase says 'the difference between the number of X that A and B have', interpret it as A - B, preserving the order of the named persons.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement references 'the difference between' two persons.
mathgap.example: Interpreting 'the difference between A and B' as B - A, reversing the sign.

mathgap.title: General Comparative Interpretation (more/fewer)
mathgap.principle: Interpret 'A has K more tomatoes than B' as A - B = K, and 'A has K fewer tomatoes than B' as A - B = -K, preserving the sign.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a comparative statement with 'more' or 'fewer' appears.
mathgap.example: Swapping the direction and writing B - A = K for 'A has K more than B', leading to sign errors.

mathgap.title: Direct Count Handling with Overrides
mathgap.principle: When a statement says 'X has N items', set X's count to N at that point, overriding any previous value (including those derived from transfers or earlier counts).
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a direct count statement appears, update the variable's value immediately.
mathgap.example: Treating a later 'X has N' as an initial count and ignoring earlier transfers that changed X's count.

mathgap.title: Chronological Transfer Application
mathgap.principle: Apply each transfer statement in the order given, subtracting the specified amount from the giver and adding it to the receiver at that moment.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a 'X gives K items to Y' statement appears.
mathgap.example: Applying a later transfer before an earlier one, or ignoring the order, resulting in incorrect final counts.

mathgap.title: Multiplicative Increase Interpretation (Factor)
mathgap.principle: When a statement says 'The number of X that Y has increases by K times', interpret it as a multiplication: new count = old count * K. For fractional K, multiply accordingly. Similarly, 'decreases by K times' means new count = old count / K.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement uses the phrase 'increases by K times' or 'decreases by K times' for a count.
mathgap.example: Treating 'increases by 9/5 times' as adding 9/5 to the count (old + 9/5) instead of multiplying, leading to wrong values.

mathgap.description: Swapped direction in 'has K more than' statements
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model often interprets 'A has K more than B' as B - A = K, reversing the intended sign.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Always map 'has K more than' to A - B = K and 'has K fewer than' to A - B = -K.

mathgap.why_it_happens: The model drops the sign when interpreting difference statements, using |A - B| instead of signed difference.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Preserve the sign and order when converting 'difference between' phrases into equations.

mathgap.description: Ignoring the chronological order of transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model applies transfers out of order or treats them as simultaneous, missing the effect of earlier overrides.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Apply transfers strictly in the order they appear in the text.

mathgap.description: Treating 'has N' as an initial count regardless of position
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model assumes direct counts are initial values and does not override them when later statements provide new counts.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: When a direct count appears later, update the variable's value, overriding any previous value.

mathgap.why_it_happens: The model interprets 'increases by K times' as addition rather than multiplication, or uses the wrong factor.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Interpret 'increases by K times' as multiplication by K; for 'decreases by K times', divide by K.
